title: Prompt Engineering Basics
description: Learn what prompts are, why they matter, and how to write clear prompts that get better results from AI systems.
learningObjectives: Identify the components of a good prompt
Write a basic prompt for a specific task

content.content: A prompt is the input you give to an AI system to guide its response. It can be a question, an instruction, a description, or a combination of all three.
Prompt: Any text input given to an AI model that shapes the model's output.
The same AI model can produce wildly different outputs depending on how you prompt it. This is why prompt engineering matters.
Effective prompts usually include four key elements: Task, Context, Constraints, and Format.
Task: What you want the AI to do (summarize, translate, explain, generate).
Context: Background information the AI needs (audience, purpose, domain).
Constraints: Rules or boundaries (length, tone, things to avoid).
Format: How you want the output structured (bullet points, JSON, essay, table).
Weak prompt: 'Tell me about AI.' Strong prompt: 'Explain what AI is in 3 bullet points for a 10-year-old, avoiding technical jargon.'
Prompt engineering is iterative. The first prompt rarely produces the best result. You refine based on what you get back.
Experienced prompt engineers treat each prompt as a hypothesis: 'If I say this, will the model do that?' Then they observe, adjust, repeat.
This is not a weakness of AI—it's the nature of working with probabilistic systems. The skill is in the refinement.

items.question: Which of these is a constraint in prompt engineering?
options: The task you want the AI to do
A rule about length or tone
items.explanation: Constraints are rules or boundaries—like length limits, tone, or things to avoid.

items.question: Rewrite this weak prompt to include context and constraints: 'Tell me about climate change.'
items.answer: Example: 'Explain the main causes of climate change in 5 bullet points for a high school student, avoiding political opinions.'
items.explanation: A good rewrite adds context (audience) and constraints (format, tone, exclusions).
